summary: INTERIM. Someone logged in to web-01 as mfischer (Mia, marketing) with her correct password from 172.58.225.22, an IP she has never used, at 19:26 and 19:30 UTC. Her real home IP (98.212.137.7) logged in separately at 19:32 while that session was still open. The 19:30 session ran the mailing export ('list newsletter', 41 customers' names and emails) and printed the whole file with cat (Mia normally looks at head -n 5). Contained: killed the session and rotated her password (rotate-secret staff-password mfischer; the help desk gives her the new one, and her SSH keys still work). No persistence found. The account can't read the shop secrets; its only sudo right is the export tool. Note: the 41-customer newsletter list should be treated as exposed. Not an intrusion: the daily deploy password logins from 64.227.126.70 are the old monitoring box listed in the deploy-password vault entry. Weaknesses fixed so far: web-01: removed 'deploy NOPASSWD sudo rsync' (instant root); root's larkspur-orders job no longer includes or evals the deploy/www-data-writable wp-config.php; the mailing-export tool no longer writes or chowns as root in the user's home (symlink attack); PHP is blocked under wp-content/uploads; the unauthenticated ?asup= endpoint of the Blue Ridge agency-support mu-plugin (showed DB host/user, deleted cache) now needs a logged-in admin; locked the jpark account (not in staff list, was in sudo and a WP admin, being brute-forced from the internet) on web-01 and ci-01. ci-01: root's maint job ran git gc on a repo whose hooks and config the developers group can write (root for any contractor), so it now runs as deploy with hooks disabled; removed the dormant 'curl web-01 | sh as root' maint mode and the ssh -A release mode; the repo config holding the GitHub token is no longer world-readable. Release, dumps, payouts and the website were checked after each change.

COMPROMISE of mfischer's account (Mia, marketing) on web-01. The intruder had both her password and her laptop SSH key (mia@air-2021).
- 19:26 and 19:30 UTC: password logins from 172.58.225.22, an IP she has never used. Her real home IP (98.212.137.7) logged in separately at 19:32. The intruder ran the mailing export 'list newsletter' (41 customers' names and emails) and printed the whole file with cat (Mia normally uses head -n 5).
- I killed the session and rotated her password (rotate-secret staff-password mfischer).
- 19:38 and 19:40: the intruder came back with the mia@air-2021 key, which had never been used in 14 days of logs, from 174.62.165.174, and exported and printed 'list recent' (52 customers).
- I removed that key from her authorized_keys (backup in /root), killed the sessions, and dropped both IPs at web-01's firewall.
- Her iPad key and the new password from the help desk still let her work.
Exposed: customer names and emails from the newsletter and recent-buyer lists. Mia's laptop is probably compromised and should be checked before she uses it again. No persistence found (no cron, no keys added, nothing in /tmp), and nothing the account could reach held a shop secret. That account was never seen on db-01 or ci-01. Not an intrusion: the deploy password logins from 64.227.126.70 are the old monitoring box listed in the deploy-password vault entry.
Weaknesses fixed:
- web-01: removed 'deploy NOPASSWD sudo rsync' (instant root).
- web-01: root's larkspur-orders job no longer includes or evals the deploy/www-data-writable wp-config.php (it reads it as www-data).
- web-01: the mailing-export tool now writes the CSV as the requesting user, which closes a symlink attack that gave root.
- web-01: nginx denies PHP under wp-content/uploads.
- web-01: the agency-support mu-plugin's ?asup= endpoint (showed DB host/user, deleted cache) now needs a logged-in admin.
- web-01: deploy's CI key accepted only from ci-01.
- web-01 and ci-01: locked jpark (not in the staff list, was in sudo and a WP admin, brute-forced from the internet).
- ci-01: root's maint job ran git gc on a repo whose hooks and config the developers group can write (root for contractors). It now runs as deploy with hooks disabled, and the hooks dir is root-owned.
- ci-01: removed the dormant 'curl web-01 | sh as root' maint mode and the ssh -A release mode.
- ci-01: the repo config holding the GitHub token is no longer world-readable.
Still open, for Maria: password SSH is enabled on all hosts (several staff use only passwords); node exporter :9100 is public; the GitHub token sits in the repo config (consider a credential helper).
Release, maint, dumps (19:40 archive arrived on ci-01), payouts, orders and the website were all checked working after the changes.

FINAL. COMPROMISE of mfischer's account (Mia, marketing) on web-01. The intruder had both her password and her laptop SSH key (mia@air-2021).
